items.title: Quoting Ted Sanders
items.summary: In general, LLM performance is incredibly multidimensional. There's no guarantee of a fixed ordering where the model that is best at math is also the model that's best at jokes. Despite that complexity, much of the variation in performance is explained by just a single variable: model size. In general, models that are bigger will (a) be more performant / reliable, (b) cost more per token, and (c) have better recall of esoteric facts. As you note, our models are ordered: Luna < Terra < Sol < Astra [ ... ] These days, version number signifies a few things at once: the order of release, the relationship to other releases, and the magnitude of improvement. So something like 6.1 would indicate it was launched after 5.6, may share some similarities to other 6.1 models in terms of train…

items.summary: If your work does not benefit from current AI tooling, that is a finding, not a failing. items.title: Game Boy Color on My Conference Badge
items.summary: Game Boy Color on My Conference Badge I'm at GitHub Universe this week and, similar to last year , the conference badge is a full-blown color screen computer. I've been hacking around with it again, and then I ran into with Steve Francia... who worked with Gemini to get a full NES emulator working on it, and then went a step further and deployed an emulator for both the Game Boy and the Game Boy Color. Which means, if you can obtain the ROM, you can run The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening on your conference badge! A neat feature of the badge is that you can turn it upside down and then use game controller touch buttons that are built into the badge body.
